question: During the Massachusetts CDL Basic Control Skills test, which categories does the examiner use to score your exercises?
choice_a: Pull-ups, encroachments, looks, and final position
choice_b: Pre-trip inspection, coupling, and parking
choice_c: Fuel efficiency, idle time, and gear selection
choice_d: Speed, braking distance, signaling, and mirror use
explanation: The manual states that during the Basic Control Skills test exercises you will be scored for pull-ups, encroachments, and looks, and separately describes final position as a scored element for the backing exercises.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: In the Basic Control Skills test, what is scored as a "pull-up"?
choice_a: Pulling the parking brake before starting an exercise
choice_b: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position
choice_c: Any forward movement made during the Forward Offset Tracking exercise
choice_d: Pulling into the stop box on the Forward Stop exercise
explanation: The manual defines a pull-up as pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position, applying to Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing).
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: According to the manual, which action does NOT count as a pull-up during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Stopping without changing direction
choice_b: Changing direction to gain a better position while backing
choice_c: Pulling forward during Reverse Offset Backing to correct your position
choice_d: Pulling forward to clear an encroachment while backing
explanation: The manual explicitly states, "Stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up."
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: How does the manual treat initial pull-ups versus an excessive number of pull-ups during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Pull-ups are always scored as encroachments instead
choice_b: Any pull-up at all results in automatic failure
choice_c: You are not penalized for initial pull-ups, but an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors
choice_d: Pull-ups are only permitted during Exercise 1, Forward Stop
explanation: The manual states you will not be penalized for initial pull-ups; however, an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: What is scored as an "encroachment" during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Sounding the horn before finishing an exercise
choice_b: Failing to check traffic before beginning to back up
choice_c: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than mirrors or unique vehicle parts at or higher than door mirror height
choice_d: Exceeding the posted speed limit inside the exercise area
explanation: The manual defines an encroachment as touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of your vehicle, other than the vehicle's mirrors or other unique vehicle parts at or higher than door mirror height.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: A vehicle has a unique part (such as on a bucket truck) that is BELOW door mirror height and it touches a boundary cone. How is this treated under the manual's encroachment rule?
choice_a: It is never counted, regardless of height
choice_b: It only counts if it happens twice in the same exercise
choice_c: It is scored as a pull-up instead of an encroachment
choice_d: It is counted as an encroachment
explanation: The manual specifies that unique parts below door mirror height are counted as an encroachment, unlike mirrors or parts at or higher than door mirror height, which are excluded.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: In the Basic Control Skills test, what is scored as a "look"?
choice_a: Opening the door or moving from a seated position while performing an exercise to check the vehicle's position
choice_b: Glancing at a cone before starting to back up
choice_c: Looking at the examiner while receiving instructions
choice_d: Checking your mirrors before an exercise begins
explanation: The manual states that if you open the door or move from a seated position when in physical control of the vehicle (or on a bus, walk to the back to get a better view), you will be scored for a look.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

topic: Safely Exiting the Vehicle During Backing
question: Before exiting the vehicle to check its position during a backing exercise, what must the applicant do?
choice_a: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral, and maintain three points of contact while facing the vehicle
choice_b: Shut off the engine entirely before opening the door
choice_c: Sound the horn twice, then open the door without stopping the vehicle
choice_d: Ask the examiner to step out and check the position instead
explanation: The manual requires that when entering/exiting the vehicle you must set your parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral, and safely exit/enter by facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact at all times.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 12, Basic Control Skills Test

question: What may result if an applicant opens the vehicle door while the vehicle is still moving (not in neutral/park) during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Only an encroachment being scored
choice_b: A single look being scored, with no further consequence
choice_c: An automatic failure for an unsafe act
choice_d: A verbal warning from the examiner with no scoring impact
explanation: The manual states that if you open your door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park), it may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: How many free looks does the manual allow to check the vehicle's position on Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) compared to Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)?
choice_a: No free looks are allowed on either exercise
choice_b: Unlimited free looks on both exercises
choice_c: One free look on Exercise 2 and two free looks on Exercise 4
choice_d: Two free looks on Exercise 2 and one free look on Exercise 4
explanation: The manual states you may be allowed a maximum of one free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-line Backing, and two free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, to check the position of your vehicle.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: What must an applicant do upon completion of a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: Turn off the engine and wait for further instructions
choice_b: Immediately exit the vehicle to notify the examiner
choice_c: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and sound the horn
choice_d: Flash the headlights twice
explanation: The manual instructs that upon completion of an exercise, you must set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and sound the horn to indicate you have completed the exercise.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring

topic: Order of Basic Control Skills Exercises
question: In what order does the manual list the four Basic Control Skills test exercises?
choice_a: Reverse Offset Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Stop
choice_b: Straight-Line Backing, Forward Stop, Reverse Offset Backing, Forward Offset Tracking
choice_c: Forward Offset Tracking, Reverse Offset Backing, Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing
choice_d: Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, Reverse Offset Backing
explanation: The manual lists the exercises as Step 1 - Forward Stop, Step 2 - Straight-Line Backing, Step 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, and Step 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 12, Basic Control Skills Test

question: What is NOT allowed while performing Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Using the turn signal before steering left
choice_b: Checking mirrors while moving through the opening
choice_c: Stopping, backing up, or exiting the vehicle during the exercise
choice_d: Changing gears while moving forward
explanation: The manual states you are NOT allowed to stop, back-up, or exit the vehicle during the Forward Offset Tracking exercise; if you stop, the exercise will be ended.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 12.2.3, Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: During Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing, what must the applicant do if they back beyond the rear boundary of the alley?
choice_a: Continue backing until told otherwise
choice_b: Immediately exit the vehicle and manually reposition it
choice_c: Pull straight forward past the alley entrance until signaled by the examiner to stop, before resuming the exercise
choice_d: The exercise automatically ends in failure with no chance to correct
explanation: The manual states that if you back beyond the rear boundary of the alley, you will be required to pull straight forward past the alley entrance until you are signaled by the examiner to stop, prior to resuming the exercise.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 12.2.4, Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: During the on-road driving test, which of the following is a requirement stated in the manual?
choice_a: Maintain a constant speed regardless of posted limits
choice_b: Wear your safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws
choice_c: Keep one hand off the wheel at all times to demonstrate control
choice_d: Complete the route in the shortest possible time
explanation: The manual states that at all times during the test you must drive in a safe and responsible manner, wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13, On-Road Driving

question: What happens if the on-road test route does not include a certain traffic situation, such as a railroad crossing?
choice_a: You may be asked to simulate the traffic situation by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing
choice_b: The test is rescheduled to a route that includes it
choice_c: The examiner skips scoring that category entirely
choice_d: You automatically fail that portion of the test
explanation: The manual states that if your test route does not have certain traffic situations, you may be asked to simulate a traffic situation by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing if you were in that traffic situation.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1, How You Will Be Tested

question: As you approach a turn, when does the manual say "unsafe coasting" occurs?
choice_a: When your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle
choice_b: Whenever your vehicle exceeds 20 miles per hour
choice_c: When you brake more than once before completing the turn
choice_d: When you fail to use your turn signal at least 100 feet before the turn
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring when your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.1, Turns

topic: Turns - Safe Gap Behind a Vehicle
question: If you must stop behind another vehicle before making a turn, how does the manual define a safe gap?
choice_a: Stopping where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you
choice_b: Stopping wherever traffic allows, with no specific reference point
choice_c: Stopping at least three car lengths behind the vehicle ahead
choice_d: Stopping close enough to read the license plate of the vehicle ahead
explanation: The manual states that if stopping behind another vehicle, you should stop where you can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of you as a safe gap.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.1, Turns

question: According to the manual, what should you do while actually making a turn?
choice_a: Release one hand from the wheel to signal pedestrians
choice_b: Keep both hands on the steering wheel and keep checking your mirror to make sure the vehicle does not hit anything on the inside of the turn
choice_c: Shift gears mid-turn to maintain engine power
choice_d: Accelerate quickly to clear the intersection as fast as possible
explanation: The manual instructs that when ready to turn, you should keep both hands on the steering wheel during the turn and keep checking your mirror to make sure the vehicle does not hit anything on the inside of the turn.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.1, Turns

question: According to the manual, what should you avoid doing while driving through an intersection?
choice_a: Changing lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_b: Checking traffic thoroughly before entering
choice_c: Yielding to pedestrians in the intersection
choice_d: Keeping your hands on the wheel
explanation: The manual states that when driving through an intersection you should decelerate and yield to any pedestrians and traffic in the intersection, and do not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.2, Intersections

question: During the Urban Business portion of the on-road test, what does the manual say about your lane position and speed?
choice_a: Lane position does not matter as long as you avoid other vehicles
choice_b: You should drive at least 10 mph under the posted speed limit at all times
choice_c: Your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane) and keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit
choice_d: You should straddle the center line to maximize visibility
explanation: The manual states that during Urban Business driving your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane) and you should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.3, Urban Business

question: What is the correct sequence for changing lanes during the on-road test, per the manual?
choice_a: Make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so
choice_b: Change lanes immediately, then check mirrors afterward
choice_c: Change lanes only when directed by another vehicle's signal
choice_d: Signal first, then check traffic only after beginning to move into the new lane
explanation: The manual instructs that during lane changes you should make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.4, Lane Changes

question: According to the manual, what should you do before entering an expressway?
choice_a: Accelerate to maximum speed before merging
choice_b: Check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic
choice_c: Merge without signaling to avoid confusing other drivers
choice_d: Come to a complete stop at the end of the entrance ramp
explanation: The manual states that before entering the expressway you should check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.5, Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: Once stopped for the Stop/Start maneuver, which of the following does the manual require?
choice_a: Keep the vehicle in gear with your foot on the brake the entire time
choice_b: Leave the turn signal on until instructed to resume
choice_c: Immediately exit the vehicle to inspect the tires
choice_d: Activate your four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, and remove your feet from the brake and clutch pedals
explanation: The manual states that once stopped, you must cancel your turn signal, activate your four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, move the gear shift to neutral or park, and remove your feet from the brake and clutch pedals.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.6, Stop/Start

question: When instructed to resume driving after the Stop/Start maneuver, what does the manual say you should do before steering back into traffic?
choice_a: Turn the steering wheel fully to the left before releasing the parking brake
choice_b: Check traffic from all directions, especially to the left, and not turn the wheel before the vehicle moves
choice_c: Immediately accelerate to the speed of traffic without checking mirrors
choice_d: Sound the horn continuously until a gap in traffic appears
explanation: The manual instructs that when resuming, you should check traffic from all directions, especially to the left, and that you should not turn the wheel before your vehicle moves.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.6, Stop/Start

question: What does the manual instruct you to do before entering a curve?
choice_a: Move into the oncoming lane for a wider turning radius
choice_b: Reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_c: Shift into neutral to coast through the curve
choice_d: Accelerate to maintain momentum through the curve
explanation: The manual states that before entering a curve, you should reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve, and keep the vehicle in the lane.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.7, Curve

question: According to the manual, what must all commercial drivers avoid doing while any part of their vehicle is in a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Using their turn signal
choice_b: Decelerating before reaching the crossing
choice_c: Stopping, changing gears, passing another vehicle, or changing lanes
choice_d: Checking their mirrors
explanation: The manual states that before reaching a railroad crossing, drivers should decelerate, look and listen for trains, check traffic, and not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

topic: Railroad Crossing - Bus and Placarded Vehicles
question: Per the manual, how far from the nearest rail must a bus, school bus, or vehicle displaying placards stop at a railroad crossing (unless the crossing is exempt)?
choice_a: Within 100 feet but not less than 50 feet from the nearest rail
choice_b: There is no specified stopping distance; any safe distance is acceptable
choice_c: Exactly 25 feet from the nearest rail
choice_d: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: The manual states that such vehicles should stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail at every railroad crossing (unless the crossing is exempt).
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

question: According to the manual, how far away from students must a school bus come to a complete stop for a student discharge?
choice_a: At least 10 feet away from the students at the stop
choice_b: At least 5 feet away from the students at the stop
choice_c: At least 25 feet away from the students at the stop
choice_d: There is no specific minimum distance required
explanation: The manual states that as you stop for the student discharge, you must bring the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.10, Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: What does the manual require of drivers with an unsynchronized manual transmission when shifting?
choice_a: They should pop the clutch to reduce shift time
choice_b: They must double-clutch when shifting
choice_c: They should ride the clutch to control speed on hills
choice_d: They may skip using the clutch entirely to shift faster
explanation: The manual states that if equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, you must double-clutch when shifting, and should not rev or lug the engine, ride the clutch, coast with the clutch depressed, or "pop" the clutch.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.11(a), Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Under the manual's Lane Usage guidance, where should a right turn on a road with multiple lanes be finished?
choice_a: In the lane directly to the right of the center line
choice_b: In the right-most (curb) lane
choice_c: In the left-most lane to prepare for a future left turn
choice_d: In whichever lane has the least traffic
explanation: The manual's Lane Usage guidance states that you should finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane, while a left turn on a multiple lane road should finish in the lane directly to the right of the center line.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.14(d), Lane Usage

question: What does the manual's Steering guidance say about hand position while driving during the on-road test?
choice_a: Keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting, then return both hands to the wheel once the shift is complete
choice_b: Only the right hand needs to remain on the wheel while turning
choice_c: Hand position is not scored during the on-road test
choice_d: One hand should always remain on the gearshift for quick shifting
explanation: The manual's Steering section states that you should not over or under steer the vehicle, and should keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting; once you have completed the shift, return both hands to the steering wheel.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 13.1.15, Steering
